strengths: The paper addresses an identifiable research audience interested in visual robustness and geometric generalization. Its finding that recognition varies systematically across unseen orientations offers useful information beyond aggregate OoD accuracy.

The fully-seen/restricted-seen paradigm provides a controlled experiment. Keeping the training-image count constant and evaluating the same restricted instances across diversity levels strengthens the evidence that orientation coverage across instances affects generalization.

The experimental coverage is substantial: four architectures, several object categories, five orientation distributions, and additional investigations of augmentation, pretraining, sample count, scale, and symmetry. These experiments support the qualitative observation that increased diversity can improve recognition of in-plane transformations.

The orientation heatmaps with overlaid object images communicate the central phenomenon effectively. The small-angle and in-plane components provide an interpretable framework for describing the observed patterns.
weaknesses: Necessary—narrow or substantiate the central claim. The abstract's statement that DNNs are 'only capable' of generalizing to in-plane rotations is stronger than the evidence establishes. Heatmaps and correlations demonstrate a tendency, without quantifying the absence of generalization elsewhere. The model also explicitly includes small-angle generalization. Restrict the conclusions to the tested networks and rendered instance-recognition setting, and reflect Section 7's caveat throughout. Retaining the exclusivity claim would require defining approximate in-plane neighborhoods and reporting accuracy outside these and small-angle neighborhoods, with uncertainty.

Necessary—distinguish descriptive fitting from predictive validation. Section 4 chooses parameters by maximizing Pearson correlation against the same accuracy map used to report model performance; no separate predictive evaluation is described. This supports a descriptive fit, but independent predictive claims remain unvalidated. Either evaluate fitted parameters on held-out instances, orientation regions, or experimental conditions, or explicitly present the model as descriptive. Also clarify whether correlations include in-distribution bins and report the fit specifically over OoD orientations.

Necessary—resolve inconsistencies in the quantitative model. Section 6 describes AE as ultimately the best-correlated model, whereas Figure 4c, particularly its fourth and fifth columns, and Figure 15 show conditions where A performs better. Furthermore, the printed logistic parameter grid assigns b values from 1 to 30; with inputs in [0,1] and nonnegative slopes, this limits outputs to at most 0.5, contrary to the stated intention of matching high observed accuracies. Although Pearson correlation is insensitive to overall scale, the implemented parameterization and affected interpretations need clarification and correction.

Necessary—provide essential evaluation details. Appendix B reports 200K images per dataset but does not clearly specify separate training, validation, and test counts, independent evaluation-image generation, or test support and empty-bin handling across the 20³ orientation bins. Learning rates were selected using OoD stability, without identifying a separate validation set. These omissions prevent assessment of evaluation independence and the reliability of per-orientation estimates. Specify the splits, selection procedure, bin aggregation, and confidence-interval calculation.

Optional—check sensitivity to orientation weighting. Independently uniform Euler angles do not produce uniformly distributed physical rotations on SO(3). A rotation-uniform evaluation or reweighted analysis would help establish how much aggregate accuracies and correlations depend on the chosen sampling distribution.

Optional—strengthen reuse and the exploratory cross-category result. The cross-category experiment uses only one trial, so additional repetitions would improve confidence in that extension. Providing a directly accessible archive of rendering settings, object identifiers, training configurations, and analysis code would also make the findings easier to reproduce than the current availability-upon-request statement.
